title: Product Roadmap
description: Now, next, later roadmap with timeline, themes, releases and a status dashboard.
forWho: Product teams planning a quarter or two ahead

spec.useCase: Orla Fitzgerald-Shah leads product at a small invoicing software company and uses this to show what is being built, what is next and what was dropped, with owners and dates.

business.name: Kestrel Ledger
business.describes: Invoicing and bookkeeping software for small service businesses.

tables.name: Themes
tables.describes: The few big bets the roadmap serves, and how many items of each have shipped.
tables.subject: thing

values.why: Shorten the days between sending an invoice and receiving money.
Make bookkeeping something owners finish in minutes.

values.theme_name: Work with the tools people already use
values.why: Connect banks, card readers and accountants.
Make every number right and every page fast.

tables.name: Roadmap items
tables.describes: Every planned, active and shipped item, with a horizon, a team and an owner.
tables.subject: thing

values.summary: Polite reminders before and after an invoice is due.
Customers pay from the email without logging in.
Schedule monthly or weekly invoices that send themselves.
Take a deposit up front and the balance later.
Snap a receipt and it files itself under the right expense.
Teach the app how you categorize repeat transactions.
A checklist that walks an owner through closing the month.
Give an accountant a seat without sharing a password.
Bring in-person card sales into the books each night.
Cut report load time for accounts with years of history.
Invoice in the customer’s currency and see the home total.
Send an invoice and check balances from a phone.
Simple stock counts for shops that sell goods.
Dropped: too few customers lose their connection while invoicing.

text.text: One page for what we are building, why, and when. Read it by horizon for the big picture or by timeline for dates. Owners keep their own items current.
Open any item to find a one-pager outline already waiting inside it.
The roadmap is a plan, not a promise. Dates move; the order of themes moves less often.
— being built, dates are firm to within two weeks.
— scoped and ready to start; dates are a quarter-sized estimate.
— worth keeping in view; no date should be quoted to a customer.

cells.text: About a week for one person
Two to four weeks for one or two people
More than a month or a cross-team effort

text.text: Move the card, update the target date, and write one line in the summary saying why. Dropped items stay on the board so nobody proposes them twice.
Anything a customer would notice or that we would put in release notes.
Each release bundles roadmap items. Add an item to a release from the release’s page.
Every included item has a summary customers can read
Support has the new help article
Growth has the announcement email drafted
The rollback steps are written down
